<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**17** anchor(s) derived from **4** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c36f5240f506e8feed86272a16bd98eaeebaca8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e484414426692614d590919349ec6b190c974097` — the merge of head `ecf02073fe6140406c28ff1d0c344e09eae5f8bf` into base `7c36f5240f506e8feed86272a16bd98eaeebaca8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e484414426692614d590919349ec6b190c974097 && git checkout e484414426692614d590919349ec6b190c974097
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7c36f5240f506e8feed86272a16bd98eaeebaca8 ecf02073fe6140406c28ff1d0c344e09eae5f8bf && git checkout -B drift-repro 7c36f5240f506e8feed86272a16bd98eaeebaca8 && git merge --no-ff ecf02073fe6140406c28ff1d0c344e09eae5f8bf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c36f5240f506e8feed86272a16bd98eaeebaca8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `10b05e871e13f05e2af7c2a3b2ff6a45c04752c5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.formula-cycle-refused.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-formula-dependency-order.test.ts, packages/formula/src/formula-read-order.ts, packages/formula/src/formula-read-order.test.ts, packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/formula-cycle-issues.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.object-formula-cycle.test.ts + read as cited code, not reviewed: packages/formula/src/relationship-traversal.ts and registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-find.ts, engine-security-resolvers.ts, engine-reference-name-visible.ts, record-title.ts and engine.ts (the `serveFormulaField` contract), packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts with one sibling entry, packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts. The changeset and `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx` are the prose face, the lane seat's.

Read at 2026-11-13T15:06Z. Inputs: card #33100 with its four comments (triage 6852852561, claims 6853060092 and 6853469180, dev report 6856451363), the PR body and file list, the diff `5430b4a4..10b05e87`, the check-runs on this head, the knock 6856609895 and the scope note 6856548085.

### ① Derived judgments

- Widening, runtime: a formula reading another formula reads its computed value on every caller of the plan builder (`find`, `findOne`, a projection, the write response, `evaluateFormulaField`, `serveFormulaField`, and through the last two a record title). Right: it is the card's second Expected arm, and the authoring doors already accept the shape.
- Narrowing, authoring: `os build`, `os validate` and the object door refuse an object whose formulas hold a cycle. Right, and exact at the object level: the walk finds a back edge exactly when a cycle exists, so an object is refused if and only if it holds one. Which members are named is not exact (S1).
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: right, an `expression` value that was accepted is refused.
- Not moved, as the code reads: an object in which no formula reads another gets the plan it had (`orderFormulaPlan` returns `requested` itself); a non-formula field; `validate_expression`.
- Moves the diff makes that the changeset does not list: what one gated read computes (M1); the read answer of a cycle member whose read is guarded (S2). Not a contract move, noted only: on an object where a formula reads another, formula keys are written onto the row in evaluation order, no longer declaration order.

### ② Semver level

- `minor` on `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/spec`: right under AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 (the kind `narrowed` takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves). The `!` title, the BREAKING line, `adr-0087: registered formula-cycle-refused` and the migration sentence are present; both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- The BREAKING line names the authoring refusal only. S2 is a read answer that moves in the narrowing direction and belongs beside it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head: 72, of which 60 success and 12 skipped, none failed or pending. `main` has moved two docs commits past the base the run merged against (`2c98485d`); neither touches a path of this diff.
- File surface: the ledger entry `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.formula-cycle-refused.ts` is outside the surface of claim 6853469180 ("Read-only elsewhere"). The report explains it (the ADR-0087 registration gate) and the helper's rename; the seat accepts or refuses the breach at ACCEPT. M1's fix lies outside that surface too.
- Dev open question (interim or final PR body): the body on this head carries the final Verification section.
- Out-of-scope findings: the stored computed-field write plan evaluates in declaration order (`carrier: none`, not measured) is the same defect on the write path, for the seat to file or to carry in Acceptance notes; `validate_expression` cannot see a cycle is carried by #32872.
- Not re-measured here: the changeset's first-party scan (no formula reads another formula in `examples/**`, `packages/**`, HotCRM). `Skills-docs: none` is the seat's ACCEPT; `skills/objectstack-formula` states no rule either way today.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay write). No governed path; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green.
- The lane is standing down after this card (scope note 6856548085): this verdict goes back to the card thread `session_016WV4cyKgEPHA5SnRXpmXz4`.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.formula-cycle-refused.ts`. The entry has the shape its siblings have and registers under the step the gate asks for. Its `reason` says a formula on a cycle "was never computable and read null on every row". That is not true of every cycle (S2). It says nothing of a stored object that already holds a cycle (N4).

`packages/formula/src/formula-read-order.ts`. The order is right: each formula after the formulas it reads, otherwise the order given. The cycle answer is right for a single loop and incomplete for formulas that share more than one (S1).

`packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts`. `orderFormulaPlan` holds against the code it cites. The closure is planned with the plan's own entry builder; an added formula is never sent to the driver and is cut back off a projection through `widened`; on the no-projection path every formula is already planned, so nothing is added and nothing needs cutting; entries are built per call, so marking `cycle` on one leaks nowhere; `applyFormulaPlan` judges `cycle` before it evaluates, so nothing loops. `resolveFormulaRelated`, `resolveFormulaPermissions` and the option-label reader all take the ordered plan, so an added formula's hop, `can()` map and labels are served like a named one's. What the closure changes for a reader that judges one entry alone is M1.

`packages/lint/src/formula-cycle-issues.ts` and the call in `validate-expressions.ts`. The refusal is located as the field-formula pass locates its findings and reports only declared names, as the docblock says. Its read set is not the engine's (N1).

Findings:

- **M1 must-fix (a security rule; the mechanism is withheld under `references/security-findings.md` and is with the seated security seat, `security#2`).** On `main` a formula's own plan entry says everything that evaluating it reads, and a read naming one formula computes that formula alone. On this head a read naming one formula computes every formula it reads, transitively, under the authority of that read. The rule to keep: a gate that admits a formula to a read by what the formula reads judges the plan that read will run, the formulas it reads included, and such a read answers for such a formula what it answers on `main`. One reader in `packages/objectql/src`, outside this diff, judges the single entry. Bring it under the rule in this PR and pin the unchanged answer, or keep the closure out of that read. Titles, the PR body, the changeset and the test names state the rule only.
- **S1 should-fix.** `formulaReadOrder` marks only the members of the loops its walk happens to close. A formula on a cycle that the walk reaches after another loop through the same formulas is already done is left unmarked. Read, not measured: with `f_n` reading `f_p` and `f_x`, `f_p` reading `f_n`, and `f_x` reading `f_p`, a walk from `f_n` marks `f_n` and `f_p` and leaves `f_x`, which reads its own value through `f_p` and `f_n`. A walk from `f_x` marks all three. So the engine evaluates `f_x` or not by the order the plan was requested in, the lint names it or not by declaration order, and the two seams can disagree on the same object, against "ONE answer for both seams" and the module's "names every formula that reads its own value". The object is still refused, since two members are named. Mark by strongly connected component (a member is on a cycle when its component holds more than one formula, or it reads itself) and pin the case in `formula-read-order.test.ts` in both orders.
- **S2 should-fix (declarations).** The changeset says a cycle member "reads null, as before", and the ledger entry that it "was never computable and read null on every row". A member whose read of the cycle is guarded could evaluate: the member reader counts a read inside `has()` and the optional spellings, and those answer a missing key with `false` or the fallback instead of faulting. Read, not measured: `has(record.f_self) ? record.f_self : 1` on `f_self` read `1` on `main` and reads `null` with the cycle fault on this head. Say so in the changeset beside the BREAKING line and in the entry's `reason` (the value depended on evaluation order; it is `null` now), and pin one guarded member in the engine test.
- **N1 nit.** The engine's reads are `bareFields` and the traversal receivers (`storedExpressionReads`); the lint's are `bareFields` alone. `record.f_y.x` on a formula `f_y` is a read for the engine and not for the lint. Both docblocks say the two use the same reader's answer.
- **N2 nit.** The docblock of `evaluateFormulaField` ("Narrowed to one field ON PURPOSE ... plans exactly the requested field, so the blast radius of a title lookup is the title's own declaration") is now wrong by the formulas the title reads.
- **N3 nit.** No pin for a cycle that an `objectExtensions` field closes with a declared field (the declared member is refused, the added one is not); the Acceptance note covers only a cycle made of added fields alone.
- **N4 nit.** The entry's `acceptanceCriteria` could say what its siblings say of stored rows: a published object that holds a cycle still loads and reads `null` with the cycle fault, and its next save is refused.

One must-fix. M1, S1 and S2 each earn a delta review of their fix, by this seat.

The reader now asks the plan builder for the plan of the one field, which is the builder and the request the read itself uses, so the gate and the read cannot name different formulas. It answers on any entry of that plan, the formulas the named one reads included. The pin in `packages/rest/src/data-reference-name-visible.test.ts` holds the answer of `main` for a formula that reads a formula, and it would go red on the earlier head. One edge moved with it (s1).

`packages/formula/src/formula-read-order.ts` (S1). Fixed. The evaluation order is the same post-order as before. Membership is Tarjan's components: a formula is a member when its component holds more than one formula or it reads itself, which is exactly "reads its own value". Each member is named with one shortest loop through it, found breadth-first inside its component, and both seams hand the reads in the same order, so they print the same sentence. The three-formula case of the earlier record is pinned in three key orders in `formula-read-order.test.ts` and in both declaration orders on a real engine.

`packages/lint/src/formula-cycle-issues.ts` (N1). Fixed: the lint takes the engine's read set, the fields read as values and the fields read through.

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.formula-cycle-refused.ts` (S2, N4). Fixed: `reason` no longer says every cycle member read null, and `acceptanceCriteria` says what a published object holding a cycle does. The guarded member is pinned in the engine test.

`packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts` (N1, N2). Docblocks only; they now say what the code does.

- **s1 should-fix.** A formula field with no `expression` took the catch in this gate on the earlier head, which answers that the field is not served, and now gets an empty plan, which answers that it is. Nothing is computed for such a field, so nothing is read that was not before; but the read that follows now names it, and what that read answers is not pinned and not measured here. Keep the earlier verdict (an empty plan answers as the catch does) or pin the answer the read gives. Small enough to ride any next push; its delta is this seat's.

No must-fix. M1, S1 and S2 of record 6856916894 are closed on this head.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:公式字段引用另一个公式字段时,引擎先算被引用的,再算引用方,卡片里 2 × 5 的例子现在读出 20;公式互相引用或引用自己(循环)时,`os build`、`os validate` 和对象保存/发布都会拒收,并点名是哪几个字段成环。
- 为什么改:以前引擎按声明顺序算公式,引用方排在前面时读出空值,而编辑器、`validate_expression` 和发布门禁都说合法,数据静默出错。
- 风险与回滚:拒收循环公式是收紧(Clause-② narrowing),已登记迁移说明 `formula-cycle-refused`;第一方示例和 HotCRM 里没有公式引用公式。已存的含循环对象照常加载,下次保存时被拒。回滚即撤销本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/formula/src/formula-read-order.ts`(计算顺序与成环判定)和 `packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts` 的 `orderFormulaPlan`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run src/engine-formula-dependency-order.test.ts`,全绿。
- 需要你做的:无。契约复审由 review#1 完成,三轮后通过。
- 席位意见:同意落地。这是 server 车道席6 收班前的最后一张卡。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:server#6 · head `ecf02073fe6140406c28ff1d0c344e09eae5f8bf` · 2026-11-13T17:32Z

1. **Shape:** 13 files, +898 −12: `formulaReadOrder` in `@objectstack/formula`, the ordered read plan in `@objectstack/objectql`, the cycle refusal in `@objectstack/lint`, the ADR-0087 semantic entry in `@objectstack/spec`, one docs line, pins; one changeset, `minor` on the four packages with the BREAKING line. Not Tier H (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green). Surface breach accepted: the ledger entry (the ADR-0087 registration gate asks for it) and the reference-name gate in `engine-reference-name-visible.ts` with its REST pin (the review's M1 fix).
2. **Premise measured:** re-measured by the dev on main; the card's case read null before and reads 20 now; the reviewer's three-formula cycle case and a guarded cycle member are pinned on a real engine.
